claims.text: Adding approximately 10 at.% Al to the coating will cause formation of a dense composite oxide scale.
The dense composite oxide scale will suppress elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The modified coating will prevent premature failure under normal subcritical-water operation.
The modified coating will prevent premature failure in accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
The Zircaloy-4 substrate has a nominal composition of Zr-98.2%, Sn-1.5%, Fe-0.2%, and Cr-0.1%.
The initial elemental Cr coating is approximately 4 μm thick and defect-free.
DC magnetron sputtering can produce the proposed AlTiCrZrNbTa film containing about 10 at.% Al.
The in situ oxide scale is primarily composed of Al2O3, TiO2, and Cr2O3.
The composite oxide scale limits oxygen penetration into the coating.
The composite oxide scale improves adhesion at the coating–substrate interface.
Added Al promotes preferential nucleation of Al2O3 and TiO2 because of favorable oxide-formation Gibbs energies.
Concurrent Cr enrichment stabilizes Cr2O3 in the scale.
The Al2O3–TiO2–Cr2O3 composite layer retards oxygen diffusion.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating forms a fragmented and delaminated oxide scale under elevated-temperature steam.
Relative to elemental Cr, the 10 at.% Al-modified coating will have a markedly lower oxidation rate.
Relative to elemental Cr, the modified coating will form a more continuous oxide scale with lower oxygen penetration and better adhesion.
Elemental Cr coatings on Zircaloy-4 are prone to premature failure caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion and oxide fragmentation.
The optimal Al concentration is approximately 9–14 at.%.
Efficacy is demonstrated at 1000 °C for 60 minutes and at 1100 °C for 30 minutes.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as introducing Al into elemental Cr, but the specified replacement is a six-element AlTiCrZrNbTa high-entropy alloy. Thus, the intervention changes several elements rather than isolating Al addition.
The initial-state field permits either elemental Cr or a Cr-dominant high-entropy-alloy baseline, whereas the baseline field defines the comparator specifically as elemental Cr.

Protection is claimed under both normal subcritical-water operation and accident steam, but the stated boundaries and experiment cover only 1000–1100 °C steam and include no normal-operation subcritical-water exposure.

The mechanism and falsification rule depend on reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion, but the listed compositional measurement is specifically an oxygen EDS line scan/map; no direct quantitative Cr and Zr concentration-profile or interdiffusion-coefficient measurement is specified.
The 1100 °C exposure is specified only for modified samples, so performance relative to the elemental-Cr control cannot be discriminated at that boundary.
